## Highlights

Users now land back on the page they asked for after logging in. There are no breaking changes.

### New

- **Back to the page after login.** When a logged-out visitor opens a page behind `LoginRequiredMiddleware`, ezauth remembers it in the session and sends them back there after login, instead of `EZAUTH_REDIRECT_AFTER_LOGIN`. It works for every sign-in method: the password form (with the MFA step), magic links, SMS codes, passkeys and OAuth2 in cookie mode. Your app doesn't need to change. See #228.
- **Pick the page yourself.** Post a `next` field with the login, magic link or SMS code form, or add `?next=/path` to `/auth/oauth2/{provider}/login` or `/auth/webauthn/login/begin`. It wins over the remembered page.
- **Safe by default.** Only a local path like `/billing` is followed. `//evil.com`, `https://...`, backslashes and control characters are ignored, so `next` can't become an open redirect. `util.IsSafeRedirectPath` does the check if you need it in your own code.
- **Building blocks.** The `middleware` package exports `RedirectToLogin`, `ReturnPath` and `LoginRedirectURL`, for apps that wire their own login-required middleware.

### Changed

- **The login redirect carries `?next=`.** `LoginRequiredMiddleware` now redirects to e.g. `/login?next=%2Fdashboard` instead of `/login`, so your login page can see where the user was going. Only full-page `GET`/`HEAD` requests get it, not form posts, JSON or HTMX requests.

### Upgrading

Nothing to do. There are no migrations in this release. Read more in the [sessions and middleware guide](https://josuebrunel.github.io/ezauth/guides/sessions-middleware-helpers/#returning-to-the-page-after-login).
